name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: Fitburg crew jailed; no new cut found
summary: Finnish court jailed Fitburg's captain for 42 months over Baltic cable damage on 5 Nov; no new cut found to 13 Nov
state: Helsinki District Court on 5 Nov sentenced the Fitburg's Russian captain to 42 months and its Azerbaijani boatswain to 34 months over the 31 Dec 2025 anchor-dragging that cut two Helsinki–Tallinn telecom cables; both deny wrongdoing and the captain plans to appeal (Marine Insight, 6 Nov). Searches to 13 Nov found no new cable cut or major new GNSS jamming escalation. The ruling concerns a past incident, so Watch holds rather than rising.
for_you: Internet users see little effect because traffic reroutes around single cable faults. Ship operators and pilots in the Baltic should continue to expect GNSS interference and follow national maritime and aviation notices.
rubric_hit: Watch: cable damage incident (Baltic case now in court); no new cuts and no multiple cuts isolating a region

sources.title: Marine Insight — Finland jails Fitburg captain over cable damage

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
